the stock-price behavior around the announcements of write-offs.
a fundamental issue in accounting: the relation between the economic consequences of write-offs and their market consequences.
the stock price behavior surrounding the announcement of a large and important corporate event: a write-off.

write-off disclosures are not sufficient to inform the market of the economic consequences of such announcements.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the market underreacts to the announcement of write-offs.
the market underreacts to the write-off announcements and overreacts to the earnings announcement.
the stock market is slow to adjust its valuation of firms that announce large write-offs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
write-offs are not a one-time, isolated event, but a process that continues to unfold in the years following the announcement date.
write-off announcements are associated with a substantial stock-price underperformance.
investors should not take write-offs at face value, and should be cautious when investing in firms that have recently written-off assets.
